_prompt:
You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: When a target sits inside another target's shadow root, the hiding logic walks into that root and hides content inside the outer target.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Criterion 2 ("content added inside a target stays visible") fails. A hidden sibling moved into the target container keeps aria-hidden="true". The shadow probe fails: `T.appendChild(x); await tick(); expect(x).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden')` gives `Received: aria-hidden="true"`. The light-DOM analog fails identically, so the cause is inherited from the base code path (the hiddenNodes.has check rejects the moved node and nothing un-hides it), not introduced by the shadow logic. Fix: when a node is added inside a visible target, clear its hidden state.
- [minor] Pre-existing and unchanged: with flag off and a target inside a shadow root, `document.body` itself gets aria-hidden="true" (the acceptRoot path hides root). Because of that, the new flag-off test "should not hide siblings ... when disabled" passes vacuously: its `not.toHaveAttribute` checks succeed only through inheritance. Reproduced via a probe asserting `document.body` has aria-hidden under flag off.
- [minor] Pre-existing gap: additions made while an inner call is active are never hidden, even after the inner call is cleaned up, because the outer walk is not re-run on resume. Light-DOM analog reproduces the same result. Shadow variant: `s.appendChild(n)` during inner, inner cleanup, `n` has no aria-hidden. The criteria only require hiding for additions after the inner cleanup, which passes.
- [minor] keepVisible() only protects elements passed before the observer hides them; calling it on an already-hidden shadow sibling does not unhide it. Light DOM behaves the same, so this is expected, not a regression.
